info.name: Ecom API
info.description:
Full endpoint set (Phases 1-7) for the Ecom backend (see src/app/routes/index.ts and openspec/changes/add-core-api-endpoints). Phase 1 = Catalog (Categories/Brands/Products). Phase 2 = Cart/Wishlist/Customer Addresses. Phase 3 = Checkout (Orders/Payments/Shipments). Phase 4 = Post-Purchase (Returns/Refunds/Reviews). Phase 5 = Inventory & Procurement (Warehouses/Stock/Stock Movements/Suppliers/Purchase Orders). Phase 6 = Marketing (Coupons/Campaigns/Banners). Phase 7 = Support, Notifications & Admin Governance (Support Tickets/Notifications/Store Settings/Roles & Permissions/Audit Logs).

Auth is cookie-based (better-auth.session_token + accessToken + refreshToken, all httpOnly). Run "Login" first — Postman's cookie jar holds the session automatically. Most storefront folders (Cart & Wishlist, Customer Addresses, Orders, Payments, Shipments, Returns, Reviews create, Support Tickets) need a CUSTOMER-role session; admin folders (Categories/Brands/Products admin routes, Warehouses, Suppliers, Purchase Orders, Stock, Coupons, Campaigns, Banners admin routes, Store Settings, Audit Logs) need OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF; Roles & Permissions is OWNER-only. Since only one session is active in the cookie jar at a time, switch the userEmail/userPassword variables and re-run Login when moving between a customer flow and an admin flow.

Note: registration requires email verification via OTP before login will succeed (see Register -> Verify Email flow below).

Admin routes generally split from public/customer routes at the path level (e.g. `GET /categories/admin` vs `GET /categories`), not role-conditional on the same path. Create requests have test scripts that auto-save the created id/slug/code into collection variables so later requests (in the same or a later folder) can chain off them — run folders top-to-bottom on a fresh run for the chaining to line up (a few requests, like deletes that would break a later folder's chain, are intentionally placed last within their folder with a note).

Update (close-core-api-gaps): added a generic admin/staff image-upload endpoint (Uploads folder), customer self-service order cancellation (Orders > Cancel Order), and returns now restock inventory on completion (Returns > Admin - Complete Return, requires warehouseId). Checkout also now applies the store's tax rate and free-shipping threshold automatically and validates stock against the warehouse-scoped Stock ledger — no request-shape changes for those, so no new Postman requests were needed.

Update (2026-08-25 reorganization): split into two top-level folders — "Public (Storefront)" (endpoints the ecommerce website calls) and "Private (Admin Panel)" (endpoints the admin panel calls) — each request kept in its original module sub-folder (Categories, Products, etc.), just regrouped by audience instead of one flat list. Also added: Private > Products > Admin - Create Product (multipart, with uploaded image files) and Private > Brands > Admin - Bulk Create Brands (see add-product-image-upload), and the full Private > Analytics folder (Dashboard Summary, Top Products, Sales by Category, Order Status Breakdown, Payment Breakdown, Returns/Refunds Summary — see add-dashboard-analytics-api and add-analytics-reports-api).

Update (align-admin-catalog-with-reference): attributes became SHOP-WIDE. The per-product option shape is gone — `options` on a product now selects an existing attribute and a subset of its values (`{ attributeId, valueIds }`), and the `options` a product returns is DERIVED from its variants' values rather than stored. Two Private folders' requests changed shape accordingly (Products > Create Product (selecting attribute values), Update Product Selection); the old `option*` collection variables were replaced by `attribute*` ones.

New Private folders: Attributes, Tax Rules, Shipping Rules, Collections, Bundle Deals, Tags. New requests: Uploads > Admin - Upload Video, Categories > Admin - Get Sub Categories (the surface over Category.parentId — no new model), Products > Admin - Update Product (rules, facts, collections, keywords).

Checkout changed: tax now comes from each product's tax rule and delivery from matching the destination against its shipping rule, so Public > Orders gained 'Get Checkout Quote' — call it before Place Order to show the shopper what they will actually be charged, and to learn up front when a destination cannot be delivered to. Place Order gained an optional `deliveryMethod` (DELIVERY | PICKUP).

Suggested run order for a fresh database: Attributes → Tax Rules → Shipping Rules → Collections → Bundle Deals → Categories → Brands → Products. The delete requests in each new folder are placed last within their folder because they remove ids the Products folder chains off.

Also added while checking the collection against the router (scripts/verify-postman-routes.ts): Private > Customers (the admin customer directory) and Public > Orders > Track Guest Order. All three routes predate this change and had simply never been documented.

item.name: Public (Storefront)
item.description: Endpoints the customer-facing ecommerce website calls. Most need a CUSTOMER-role session (or work as a guest via cart's guestToken cookie) except explicitly public/anonymous reads (category tree, product listing, banners, etc.) — see each request's own auth requirement.

request.description: multipart/form-data - `image` is optional; when present it's uploaded to Cloudinary server-side (see auth.controller.ts) and its URL replaces the field before saving.
No body - reads the refreshToken and better-auth.session_token cookies.

Redirect-based OAuth flow - not directly testable from Postman's request runner. Open this URL in a browser instead; it redirects through Google and back to /auth/google/success, then to FRONTEND_URL.
No auth. Where Google redirects after a successful consent. Not called directly — it completes the session and redirects on to the client. Listed so the collection matches the router.
No auth. Where the OAuth flow lands when consent fails or is cancelled. Not called directly. Listed so the collection matches the router.
No auth. Top-level ACTIVE categories with one level of ACTIVE children nested.
No auth. 404 if the category is inactive.
No auth. ACTIVE-only.
No auth. 404 if the brand is inactive.

No auth. ACTIVE-only, paginated. `category` matches the product's primary category OR a supplementary ProductCategory tag.

The search param here is `searchTerm` (not `search`) — an unrecognised filter key is ignored, so `?search=jbl` silently returns every product instead of erroring. Use this endpoint for a full search RESULTS PAGE; for a search-as-you-type dropdown use `GET /products/search?q=` instead, which is roughly 10x faster.

No auth. Fast search-as-you-type suggestions — a DIFFERENT endpoint from `GET /products?searchTerm=`.

**Note the path and the param:** it is `/products/search` with `q`, not `/products` with `search`. Sending `search=` to the listing endpoint is an unknown filter and returns every product unfiltered.

Returns only `{ id, name, slug, price, brandName, image }` — no category, brand object, or campaign pricing. That is what makes it fast: one database round trip (~77ms) against the listing endpoint's ~0.3-1.5s.

Matches product name, SKU, description AND brand name, case-insensitively. Misspellings still resolve (`ankar` finds Anker) via trigram similarity, but exact matches always rank above approximate ones. Results are ordered by relevance, not recency.

`q` is required and must be non-empty (400 otherwise). `limit` is optional and capped server-side at 8 regardless of what is requested.

No auth. Full detail incl. variants/images/attributes. Each image now includes `variantId` (string or null) indicating which variant it belongs to, so the storefront can render a variant-aware gallery. 404 if not ACTIVE.

No auth. Catalog-structure scoring: same category (+3), same brand (+2), shared supplementary category (+1), price within +/-40% (+1). Excludes the source product and non-ACTIVE products; backfills with featured/newest so the list is never empty. limit defaults to 6, clamped to 24.

Homepage 'Featured Products' row. isFeatured is parsed as a real boolean: 'false' filters to NON-featured products, it is not treated as falsy-and-ignored. ACTIVE-only, so a featured DRAFT/ARCHIVED product stays invisible.

Homepage 'Best Selling Products' row, ordered by Product.totalSold — a denormalized count of units sold, maintained only when a payment reaches PAID. A placed-but-unpaid COD order does not count. Never-sold products read 0 and sort last.
Homepage 'New Arrivals' row — the newest ACTIVE products by createdAt.

NEGATIVE TEST — expects HTTP 400.

sortBy on the PUBLIC listing is restricted to: createdAt, price, name, averageRating, totalSold. A field is sortable only if its value already appears in the public product payload.

Without this, ?sortBy=costPrice ordered the whole catalog by supplier cost and leaked every product's margin ranking to an anonymous caller. The request is rejected rather than silently falling back to the default order, which would return 200 in an order the caller never asked for and cannot detect.

The ADMIN listing (/products/admin) is deliberately unaffected.

Records that a shopper opened this product's detail page.

Always answers 202 with the same body — whether the view was counted, deduplicated as a repeat, or dropped as a bot. A response that distinguished them would let a caller probe whether a given viewer has already seen a product.

Deduplicated per viewer per product per 6-hour window, so posting this repeatedly increments `viewCount` only once. Signed-in shoppers are identified by session (optionalAuth); guests by a keyed hash of IP + user-agent — the raw address is never stored.

Check the effect with 'Public - Get Product By Slug' and read `data.viewCount`.

See add-product-view-tracking design.md.

item.name: Public - Record Product View (bot UA, counts nothing)

request.description:
NEGATIVE TEST — expects HTTP 202 with `viewCount` UNCHANGED.

Send this with a crawler User-Agent header, e.g.
    User-Agent: Googlebot/2.1

The 202 is deliberate and identical to a counted view: a crawler learns nothing from the response. Verify by reading `data.viewCount` before and after — it must not move.

item.name: Public - Record Product View (bad source, expect 400)

request.description:
NEGATIVE TEST — expects HTTP 400 and no change to `viewCount`.

`source` is a literal: only `product_detail` is accepted. It is the marker separating 'a shopper opened this page' from a listing, a preview, or a prefetch — so only the detail page can record a view. Omitting `source` entirely fails the same way.

Ranks the catalogue by lifetime views. `viewCount` joined the public sort allowlist alongside createdAt, price, name, averageRating and totalSold.

`viewCount` is a LIFETIME TOTAL — it says nothing about how many people are on a page now.

No auth required — works for guests (guestToken cookie, auto-issued/persisted by Postman's cookie jar) and logged-in customers alike. Shows a live `discount` preview if a coupon is applied (see Apply Coupon below).
find-or-increment — re-adding the same product/variant increments quantity instead of creating a duplicate line. Saves cartItemId from the first cart item.

Run the Coupons folder first so {{couponCode}} is set. Validates status/dates/usage limits/minimum order amount/product eligibility, then persists the applied coupon in an `appliedCoupon` cookie (mirrors guestToken) — GET /cart and checkout both read it back.
Clears the appliedCoupon cookie — pure cookie removal, no cart mutation.
Auth required — no guest wishlist (unlike Cart).
Auth required. Number of wishlist entries referencing an ACTIVE product - for the header badge, without transferring the items.
Auth required. Returns { inWishlist, itemId }. Always 200 - 'not saved' is an answer, not a 404. Lets a product card render its heart state without fetching the whole list.
Auth required. Removes by productId so a heart toggle needs no itemId lookup first. 404 if the product is not in the caller's wishlist.

Auth required, ownership enforced (404 otherwise). Adds to cart then removes from the wishlist. If the cart add fails the wishlist entry is left in place. An existing cart item is incremented, not duplicated.
Auth required, self-service only. Saves addressId.
Unsets any other default address of the same type.
Run after the Orders folder if you want to keep addressId valid for Place Order.

What this basket costs to this destination, WITHOUT placing anything.

Necessary because shipping is no longer a flat price the storefront can add up itself: it comes from each product's shipping rule matched against where the order is going, and so does tax. Without asking the server, checkout would show one number and charge another — or let the shopper reach Place Order before learning nobody delivers to their address.

Deliberately shares its arithmetic with Place Order, so a quote and a charge cannot drift apart.

Optional-auth, like checkout itself: a guest needs this most, having no saved address to have been quoted against before. A guest sends `country`/`state` inline instead of `shippingAddressId`; everything is optional, because a quote is asked for while the shopper is still typing.

Returns subtotal, discountAmount, taxAmount, shippingAmount, shippingBeforeWaiver (so a waived charge can be shown as a saving), deliveryDays, totalAmount, and — when every matched place offers it — pickupAmount and pickupTotalAmount. `places` carries every matched place — name, price, deliveryDays, offersPickup, pickupPrice — which is what checkout shows the shopper now that there is no delivery-method list to pick from.

An undeliverable destination is a 400 naming the PRODUCT that cannot get there, not a silent zero.

The guest form of the quote: no saved address, so the destination is sent inline as it is typed.

A partial destination is a real question rather than an error — it simply matches fewer places, falling back to the country place and then to the catch-all.

Checkout from the customer's cart — snapshots line items, validates stock/price, clears the cart on success. If a coupon is applied to the cart (see Cart & Wishlist folder), it's consumed automatically here (discount applied, Coupon.usageCount incremented) — no need to resend the code. Saves orderId.

Tax comes from EACH PRODUCT'S tax rule rather than the store-wide rate, and delivery from matching the shopper's destination against each product's shipping rule — charged once per distinct rule in the order, since products under one delivery policy travel together. A product with no rule of its own rides along in a parcel already being paid for; a basket where NOTHING carries a rule has no parcel to ride in and is refused with a 400 naming the products.

`deliveryMethod` is optional and defaults to DELIVERY. An undeliverable destination is refused with a 400 naming the product, never charged as zero.

No shipment is opened here — the admin creates one at dispatch (Private → Shipments), so an order never claims a dispatch that has not happened.

Call 'Get Checkout Quote' first to show the shopper what they will be charged.

Collection instead of delivery, charged at the matched places' `pickupPrice` rather than their delivery price.

Accepted ONLY when every matched place offers collection — an order half of which still has to be delivered is not one the shopper can collect. Otherwise 400.

Call Get Checkout Quote first: its `pickupAmount` is null when this will be refused.

Note that free shipping — from a coupon or the store's order-value threshold — waives DELIVERY only. Choosing to collect is choosing a different service, and its price is what that place charges for it.
Own orders only for a customer; every order for OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF.
Customer self-service — cancels the requester's own order while it's still PENDING or CONFIRMED. 404 if not your order, 400 if it's already PROCESSING or later. No body.

How a guest looks up an order they placed without an account.

No session, so the order number alone must not be enough — it is guessable, and would expose one customer's order to anyone. Requiring the phone the order was placed with makes the PAIR the credential.

POST rather than GET so the phone — half of that credential — stays out of URLs and server logs.

Declared above `/:id` in the router, or that path would swallow the literal 'track'.
Gateway-agnostic — records a payment attempt/result for the order.

Staff-only (OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF). Moves an existing payment to a new status — this is the transition that maintains Product.totalSold.

Before this existed, a COD payment created as PENDING at checkout had no way to become PAID, so the store could not tell a collected parcel from an uncollected one.

The counter moves on TRANSITIONS, not on calls: marking an already-PAID payment PAID again is a no-op, so a retry cannot double-count. Only a payment that had actually been PAID decrements when refunded/cancelled.
The order's shipment, once one exists. 404 — "This order has no shipment yet" — until an admin opens it at dispatch; checkout does not create one.

Customer-initiated. {{orderItemId}} isn't captured automatically anywhere in this collection — copy an `items[].id` from "Get Order By Id"'s response into this variable first. Validates against the order (incl. cumulative quantity already claimed by prior non-rejected/cancelled returns).
Own returns for a customer; every return for staff.
Verified-purchaser check: requires a DELIVERED/COMPLETED order containing this product for the requesting customer (run after Update Order Status -> DELIVERED/COMPLETED). Defaults to PENDING.
No auth. APPROVED only.
Auth required. The caller's own reviews in EVERY status, including PENDING and REJECTED which the public list hides. Supports page/limit/sortBy and filters on status, rating, productId.

Auth required, author only (404 otherwise). Editing an APPROVED review resets it to PENDING for re-moderation and removes it from the product's rating aggregate until re-approved. At least one field required.
Auth required, author only (404 otherwise). Recalculates the product's rating aggregate.
Own tickets for a customer; every ticket for staff.
Participant-scoped: the ticket's owning customer, its assignedTo staff user, or any OWNER/ADMIN.

The campaign occupying a storefront slot, with its products already priced.

An empty slot is 200 with data:null, not a 404 — 'no deal running' is an ordinary state the storefront handles by omitting the section.

endsAt is what drives the countdown, and is passed through exactly as stored: null means no deadline and must render no countdown, never a computed one.

Eligibility matches the automatic product-discount rule exactly: ACTIVE, and now inside startsAt/endsAt. When two eligible campaigns claim the same slot, the most recently started wins.

discountType/discountValue are deliberately withheld — only the resulting campaignPrice is public.
NEGATIVE TEST — expects HTTP 400. placement is validated against the CampaignPlacement enum (DEAL_OF_WEEK, FLASH_SALE); an unrecognised slot is rejected rather than silently returning empty.

No auth. Returns ACTIVE banners currently inside their startsAt/endsAt window, ordered by sortOrder ascending. With no placement filter, every region is returned. Valid placements: HEADER, MID, FOOTER, SIDEBAR, POPUP, HERO_SLIDER, HERO_SIDE, HERO_PROMO.

No auth. Narrows the listing to one storefront region. The status and scheduling rules are unchanged by the filter. Valid placements: HEADER, MID, FOOTER, SIDEBAR, POPUP, HERO_SLIDER, HERO_SIDE, HERO_PROMO.

No auth. Homepage hero region: the large left carousel (multiple banners rotate as slides). Returns every ACTIVE, in-window banner for this region ordered by sortOrder — there is NO per-region cap, so how many are displayed is the storefront's decision.

No auth. Homepage hero region: the square tiles at the top right. Returns every ACTIVE, in-window banner for this region ordered by sortOrder — there is NO per-region cap, so how many are displayed is the storefront's decision.

No auth. Homepage hero region: the wide tile beneath the square tiles. Returns every ACTIVE, in-window banner for this region ordered by sortOrder — there is NO per-region cap, so how many are displayed is the storefront's decision.
Own notifications only. Saves notificationId from the first result, if any exist.

NO AUTH. Storefront presentation payload for the header and footer: branding, mainNav, footerColumns, socialLinks, announcementBar, newsletter, contact, currency. Explicit allow-list - defaultTaxRatePercent and freeShippingThreshold are NOT exposed. Read-only: never creates or mutates the settings row.
No auth. Returns every PUBLISHED page trimmed to { id, title, slug } — the list the admin panel's link pickers and the footer editor offer as targets. DRAFT pages are never included.

No auth. Returns the PUBLISHED page at this slug, which the storefront renders at the root-level `/<slug>`.

A DRAFT page and a slug no page uses both return 404, deliberately: the response must not let a visitor tell an unpublished page from one that was never written.

item.name: Private (Admin Panel)
item.description: Endpoints the admin panel (electrode-admin) calls. All require an OWNER/ADMIN/STAFF session (Roles & Permissions is OWNER-only) — see each request/module route file for the exact role gate.

request.description: Soft delete - sets isDeleted/isActive, doesn't hard-delete the row. A user cannot delete themselves (see user.service.ts).

OWNER/ADMIN only. Plain-JSON variant: `image`/`banner` are pre-hosted URLs. For file upload instead, use the "Admin - Create Category (multipart image upload)" request below. `slug` is auto-generated from `name` if omitted. Both save categoryId/categorySlug for the rest of this folder.

OWNER/ADMIN only. multipart/form-data variant of category create: the `data` field carries the same JSON payload the plain-JSON request uses (WITHOUT `image`/`banner`), and the `image`/`banner` file fields hold the images. The server uploads them to Cloudinary and stores the returned URLs. Select an actual image file for the `image` field before sending — Postman can't pre-fill a file picker. `banner` is optional (left disabled here). A plain-JSON request with `image`/`banner` URLs still works too.
Child of {{categoryId}} - demonstrates the parent/child hierarchy. Saves childCategoryId.
OWNER/ADMIN only. Flat, paginated, every status (unlike the public tree endpoint below).
OWNER/ADMIN only. Full hierarchy (every status, unlimited depth), nested via children at every level — unlike the flat/paginated list above.

The sub-category list. NO new endpoint or model was needed: the hierarchy has always lived on `Category.parentId`, and `parentId` was already in this listing's filterable fields — what was missing was only an admin surface for it.

The admin panel's 'Sub categories' page is this request plus a parent picker.

OWNER/ADMIN only. multipart/form-data variant of category update: `data` carries the JSON patch (WITHOUT `image`/`banner`), and the `image`/`banner` file fields upload new images. Old images are deleted from Cloudinary when replaced. Select an actual image file for the `image` field before sending.
Deletes the child category (not the parent, so categoryId/categorySlug stay valid for the rest of the folder/Products requests below).

OWNER/ADMIN only. Plain-JSON variant: `logo` is a pre-hosted URL. For file upload instead, use the "Admin - Create Brand (multipart logo upload)" request below. Both save brandId/brandSlug for the rest of this folder.

OWNER/ADMIN only. multipart/form-data variant of brand create: the `data` field carries the same JSON payload the plain-JSON request uses (WITHOUT `logo`), and the `logo` file field holds the image. The server uploads it to Cloudinary and stores the returned URL as `logo`. Select an actual image file for the `logo` file field before sending — Postman can't pre-fill a file picker. A plain-JSON request with a `logo` URL still works too.

OWNER/ADMIN only. Creates one brand per name (status: true, no description/logo). Blank names, in-batch duplicates, and names matching an existing brand (case-insensitive) are skipped, not failed — response reports created[] and skipped[] (with reason) separately.
OWNER/ADMIN only. Plain-JSON variant. To replace the logo with an uploaded image, use "Admin - Update Brand (multipart logo upload)" below.

OWNER/ADMIN only. multipart/form-data variant of brand update: `data` carries the JSON patch (WITHOUT `logo`), and the `logo` file field uploads a new logo. The old logo is deleted from Cloudinary when replaced. Select an actual image file for the `logo` field before sending.
Run this only after the Products folder - Products' "Create Product" request references {{brandId}}.

item.name: Attributes
item.description:
Shop-wide axes of choice — Colour, Size, Weight — defined once and reused on any product.

Admin-only throughout: a shopper meets an attribute through a product's options, never as a catalogue of its own.

Replaces the per-product ProductOption/ProductOptionValue model. Run the two create requests first — the rest of this folder, and the Products folder's option requests, chain off the ids they save.

request.description:
OWNER/ADMIN only. Defines Colour once for the whole shop.

`values` order IS the presentation order — position is taken from array order rather than sent explicitly, so two values cannot claim the same position.

`presentation` decides how values are drawn: SWATCH uses each value's `swatch` colour, LABEL shows its text. Declared here rather than guessed from the name, which would break on 'Color' vs 'Colour'.

Saves attributeColourId, attributeValueRedId, attributeValueGreenId.

OWNER/ADMIN only. Authored S, M, XL in that order — nothing about the labels themselves says S precedes M, which is exactly why order is stored rather than derived.

Saves attributeSizeId and the three value ids.

Expect 409. The unique index is exact, so 'Colour' and 'colour' would both be allowed by the database — and the merchant would then face two attributes that look identical, which is precisely the confusion moving attributes shop-wide exists to end. The service compares case-insensitively.

item.name: Admin - Get All Attributes (unpaginated, for pickers)

request.description:
Every attribute with its values, ordered by position then name. What the admin product form fills its checkboxes from — a picker that paginated would hide half the shop's attributes behind a page control.

Declared above `/:id` in the router, or the literal 'all' would be captured as an id.
Paginated list for the Attributes admin page. Searchable on `name`, filterable on `presentation`.
Includes `values` ordered by position.

Values carrying an `id` are UPDATED; those without are created. Anything omitted is DELETED — send the full intended set, exactly as variants and images already work.

Renaming a value here changes it for every product selling it, and loses no variants: the variant points at the value id, not at its label.

item.name: Admin - Update Attribute (remove a value products sell, expect 409)

request.description:
Expect 409 once a product sells Green — the message names how many products are affected.

Checked BEFORE the transaction opens, so a refused request modifies nothing. Confirm with `?force=1` (next request) to go ahead anyway.
The same edit, confirmed. Products selling the removed value lose those choices — which is why the unconfirmed call refuses rather than doing it quietly.

Expect 409 while products still sell its values, with a count of how many.

Deleting cascades to every variant selection built on it, so this guard is the one thing standing between a routine catalog edit and a shop full of unbuyable products.
Placed last in this folder: it removes the attribute the Products folder chains off. Run the Products option requests first.

item.name: Tax Rules
item.description:
Named tax charges assigned per product, replacing the single shop-wide rate on StoreSetting.

Admin-only: a shopper is told what tax cost at checkout, where it is computed, and never needs the rule itself.

request.description:
A PERCENT rule applies to the price ACTUALLY charged, so a discounted product is taxed on the discounted amount rather than the list price.

Saves taxRuleId.

A FLAT rule charges its amount PER UNIT bought, not per line — a fixed tax on a product is a tax on each one.

Saves taxRuleReplacementId, used as the reassignment target below.

item.name: Admin - Get All Tax Rules (unpaginated, for pickers)

request.description: Every rule, for the product form's picker.
Searchable on `name`, filterable on `type`.

item.name: Admin - Get Tax Rule By Id

request.description: A single rule.
Changing the rate changes what every product assigned to it is taxed.

item.name: Admin - Delete Tax Rule in use (expect 409)

request.description: Expect 409 with a count of the products using it. A product must be taxable, so it cannot simply lose its rule — the foreign key is Restrict for exactly that reason.

item.name: Admin - Delete Tax Rule (reassigning its products)

request.description:
The merchant names the replacement, and the move happens in the SAME transaction as the delete — so no product is ever briefly without a rule.

Placed last in this folder: it removes the rule the Products folder chains off.

item.name: Shipping Rules
item.description:
Named delivery policies made of places, assigned per product. A place prices one destination, so delivering across the city is not charged the same as delivering across the country.

A rule MUST always keep at least one place: one matching nowhere can charge nothing, and its products would be undeliverable.

item.name: Admin - Create Shipping Rule (region, country, catch-all)

request.description:
Three places, most specific to least. Matching at checkout is region → country → all-destinations: without that order two places covering the same shopper would be a coin toss, and a merchant adding a specific rate would see it ignored at random.

`country`/`state` omitted means 'anywhere' — the third place here is the catch-all, and is what lets the rule deliver somewhere it has not enumerated.

`offersPickup` lets a shopper collect in person at `pickupPrice` instead of having it delivered.

Saves shippingRuleId.
Saves shippingRuleReplacementId, used as the reassignment target below.

item.name: Admin - Create Shipping Rule (region without a country, expect 400)

request.description: Expect 400. A region without a country is meaningless — 'Dhaka' in which country? — and could never be matched against a shopper's address.

item.name: Admin - Create Shipping Rule (two places, same destination, expect 400)

request.description: Expect 400. Two places covering the same destination would make matching a coin toss, and the merchant would never know which price a shopper saw.

item.name: Admin - Get All Shipping Rules (unpaginated, for pickers)

request.description: Every rule with its places, for the product form.
Places come back ordered most-specific-first, which is also the order the matcher wants.

item.name: Admin - Get Shipping Rule By Id

request.description: A single rule with its places.
Places with an `id` are updated, those without are created, and existing places absent from the payload are deleted — the same replace-the-set contract as variants and images.

item.name: Admin - Update Shipping Rule (remove every place, expect 400)

request.description: Expect 400. Enforced in the Zod schema AND again in the service, since an update reaching it by another path could otherwise leave a rule matching nowhere and make its products undeliverable.

item.name: Admin - Delete Shipping Rule in use (expect 409)

request.description: Expect 409 with a count. Same reasoning as tax rules: a product must be deliverable, so it cannot simply lose its rule.

item.name: Admin - Delete Shipping Rule (reassigning its products)

request.description: The move and the delete share one transaction. Placed last in this folder: it removes the rule the Products folder chains off.

item.name: Collections
item.description:
Merchandising groupings independent of the category tree — "Top selling", "Eid specials". Categories answer "what is this"; collections answer "why are we showing it".

A product belongs to any number and keeps its category regardless.

request.description: `slug` is derived from `name` when omitted. Saves collectionId.

item.name: Admin - Get All Collections (unpaginated, for pickers)

request.description: Every collection, for the product form's multi-select.
Searchable on `name` and `slug`, filterable on `isVisible`.
A single collection.

request.description:
OWNER/ADMIN only. Creates the Product together with its nested variants/images/attributes in one call. Saves productId/productSlug/variantId/imageId/attributeId for the rest of this folder.

Update (align-admin-catalog-with-reference): `taxRuleId` and `shippingRuleId` are required in practice — a product must be taxable and deliverable. `bundleDealId` is optional (null clears it). `collectionIds` and `tags` are the FULL intended sets, replacing what was there; omitting either key leaves it alone. `tags` names are created on demand and de-duplicated case-insensitively, which is why there is no tag create endpoint.

`isRefundable`/`hasWarranty` are TRI-STATE: null means the merchant has not said, which the storefront renders as nothing at all — a different claim from false.

`unit` is what is being sold ('1 kg', '500 ml'), `badge` a short storefront label ('New', 'Hot'). `video`/`videoThumbnail` come from Uploads > Admin - Upload Video.

item.name: Admin - Create Product (multipart, with uploaded image files)

request.description: OWNER/ADMIN only. multipart/form-data variant of product create: the `data` field carries the same JSON payload the plain-JSON request uses, plus an optional `imageSlots` array ({altText?, sortOrder?, isPrimary?, variantIndex?}) matched by position to the uploaded files under the repeated `images` field (max 10). Select actual image files for the two `images` file fields before sending — Postman can't pre-fill a file picker. See openspec/changes/add-product-image-upload and link-product-images-to-variants.

item.name: Admin - Update Product (rules, facts, collections, keywords)

request.description:
The fields this change added, on their own.

`bundleDealId: null` CLEARS the offer; omitting the key leaves it as it was. `collectionIds: []` removes every membership — these are full intended sets, not additions.

`tags` here sends 'wireless' twice in different cases on purpose: the product ends up carrying it ONCE. De-duplication is exact and case-insensitive, which is what stops 'Wireless' being created beside 'wireless'.

`hasWarranty: null` means 'not stated' and shows nothing on the storefront — distinct from `false`, which is a claim that there is no warranty.

Demonstrates the nested create-update-delete sync: {{variantId}} is updated, a new variant (no `id`) is created, and any other existing variant not listed here is deleted. Images are synced too: existing images keep their `id` and can be reassigned by `variantId` or cleared by omitting the field; new images without `id` are created.

item.name: Admin - Get All Products (sorted by views)

request.description:
Backs the Views column in the admin product list.

Ascending puts the least-viewed products first, which is the question the column exists to answer: a product nobody finds, as distinct from one many people find and reject. Sorting is server-side because the list is paginated — sorting in the browser would only reorder the current page.

Admin listings are deliberately NOT restricted to the public sort allowlist.

BREAKING CHANGE from the previous shape. A product no longer DEFINES its options — it SELECTS values from shop-wide attributes. Run the Attributes folder first.

`options[].attributeId` names an existing attribute; `valueIds` are the subset of its values this product sells, in the order to present them. Nothing here creates an attribute or a value; the service checks that every value named really belongs to the attribute named.

`optionValueIndexes` still selects one value PER OPTION, by index into that option's `valueIds` — positional because a variant's selection is not yet stored on create, the same reason images use `variantIndex`. So `[1, 2]` means Colour=Green (index 1), Size=XL (index 2).

This deliberately does NOT create all 6 combinations: not every combination is a real product. Green/S and Green/M simply do not exist, and the storefront shows those values as unavailable rather than hiding them.

Note the response's `options` is DERIVED, not stored — the backend rebuilds it from the attributes these variants' values belong to, so the storefront keeps the shape it already resolves against.

See align-admin-catalog-with-reference design.md.

item.name: Admin - Update Product Selection (add a value, add a variant)

request.description:
Sells one more size (XXL) and adds a variant using it, keeping the existing one.

Add XXL to the SIZE ATTRIBUTE first (Attributes > Admin - Update Attribute) — a product cannot invent a value, only select one. Then set attributeValueXxlId from that response.

Variants carrying an `id` are UPDATED and keep their stock, price, code and images; those without are created. Anything omitted is DELETED — send the full intended set.

Keeping the `id` is the important part: it is what makes the backend update the row rather than delete and recreate it, and so what preserves its images and its links from past orders. This is the defect that started this change — regeneration used to match rows by index and silently reset four variants to zero stock.

`optionValueIndexes` refers to positions in THIS request's `valueIds`, not to stored ones: XXL is index 3 because it is fourth in the Size values sent here.

A change that would remove a variant appearing on a past order is refused before the transaction opens, naming the variant.

item.name: Admin - Create Product (incomplete option selection, expect 400)

request.description:
NEGATIVE TEST — expects HTTP 400. Nothing is created.

The variant selects a value for Colour but not for Size. A variant must select EXACTLY ONE value per option of its product: that invariant is what lets a two-option selection resolve to a single row, and it cannot be expressed as a database constraint, so the service enforces it.

The check runs before the transaction opens, so a rejected request creates no product, option, value or variant.

Related rejections, all 400:
  - an index out of range for its option's values
  - two variants selecting the same combination (resolution would be ambiguous)
  - duplicate option names, or duplicate value labels within an option
  - a selection sent for a product that declares no options

Creates a campaign. Its discounts apply automatically to the tagged products on every public product read once the campaign is ACTIVE and inside its startsAt/endsAt window — customers need no code.

`placement` is optional and opt-in: it puts the campaign into a storefront slot (DEAL_OF_WEEK, FLASH_SALE) so `GET /campaigns/active?placement=` can find it. This is what fills the homepage 'Deal of the Week' row and gives its countdown a real deadline — set `endsAt` for that. Omit `placement` and the campaign still discounts its products, it just occupies no slot.

Placement is NOT unique: a successor campaign can be scheduled while the current one runs. When two eligible campaigns share a slot, the one with the most recent startsAt is served.

OWNER/ADMIN only. Upserts the one StoreSetting row — never creates a second one.

Every field is optional and the patch is partial: a key left out leaves that column untouched. That is what lets the separate admin editors (Store Settings, Header Links, Footer Links, Checkout Setting, Site Setting) write to this one endpoint without clobbering each other.

checkoutConfig — two invariants are rejected with a 400: no field may be hidden and required at the same time, and "phone" must stay shown and required (guest order lookup and the per-phone COD cap are keyed on it).

theme — colours must be hex (#rgb or #rrggbb). "maxWidth" is 960-2560, or the string "full". "font" is sent as the text pasted from Google Fonts (the @import rule, the <link> tag, or the bare URL); the server parses it, rejects any host other than fonts.googleapis.com, and stores a rebuilt URL. Reading the settings back returns "font" as an object of { family, url }.
NOTE: checkAuth gates routes by Role.name string, not RolePermission — this manages RBAC data for a future finer-grained check, it doesn't itself change what any route allows.
